summary: Command injection through the git scope argument of the audit tool
details:
code-auditor-mcp is a Model Context Protocol server that performs static analysis of source code. Its audit tool accepts a `scope` argument. When the value begins with `git:`, the remainder is treated as a git reference and passed without validation into ``execSync(`git diff --name-only ${ref}`)``, which runs through a shell.

A caller who can influence the `scope` argument can therefore run arbitrary shell commands with the privileges of the server. In an AI agent the tool arguments are produced by a language model, and a model can be steered by content it reads, such as a web page, an issue, or a file in the repository being audited. The tool's own description tells the model that it may pass `git:<ref>`.

Version 4.1.0 validates the reference against an allowlist pattern, invokes git through `execFileSync` with an argument array so that no shell interprets it, and passes `--end-of-options` so that a reference beginning with a hyphen cannot be read as a git option.

The affected range was established by testing candidate releases. The git scope feature and the vulnerable call first appear in 3.0.0, releases up to and including 2.6.2 contain neither, and 4.0.4 is the last affected release.

database_specific.deployer_note: The scope argument is written by the model, so content the agent reads while auditing, such as a file in the repository or an issue comment, can steer it. Where an agent may already run any shell command without approval, this adds little. Where shell commands need approval, or the agent is limited to approved tools, however, the flaw runs a command nobody was asked to approve, because the prompt shows an audit request and not the shell command inside it. Upgrade to 4.1.0 or later, and treat any repository the agent did not write as untrusted input.
